# TBC Uzbekistan Deploys Full-Scale AI Platform, Reducing Customer Interaction Costs by Over 90%

Published at September 25th 2026, 3:14 PM EDT via Worldnewswire

In early 2025, TBC Bank Uzbekistan launched one of the most comprehensive artificial intelligence programs undertaken by any financial institution in Central Asia. Running from January through November and requiring over 45,000 man-hours of development work, the TBC Uzbekistan AI Platform Program addressed a fundamental challenge: how to build an independent AI foundation, integrate it across core business processes, and embed an AI-first culture across the organization — all simultaneously. The result is a program that has already delivered substantial financial returns, reshaped the bank’s cost structure, and established durable infrastructure for long-term competitive advantage in a rapidly evolving digital market.

# How Intact is measuring AI’s annual benefits 

 iStock.com/Phiwath Jittamas 

Intact Financial Corporation (IFC) is seeing clear financial gain from its use of artificial intelligence (AI), “in aggregate currently producing north of $220 million of recurring benefit annually that we can measure,” IFC chief operating officer Patrick Barbeau said Thursday.

About a year-and-a-half ago, Intact anticipated the number would grow to $500 million by 2030, but has since revised that estimate to $500 million in annualized financial benefits by 2028, Barbeau said during a fireside chat at the 27 th annual Scotiabank Financials Summit in Toronto.

“We’ve accelerated our investment recently, and we’re saying that the benefit on the pricing and risk selection side in commercial and specialty lines is actually producing [a] better outcome than we even anticipated at the time,” Barbeau says.

# Prudential Hong Kong launches AI underwriting tool with Alibaba Cloud

Peter Sonner

 Sep 28, 2026

Prudential Hong Kong has fully launched an AI-powered underwriting tool developed with Alibaba Cloud, giving financial consultants preliminary underwriting guidance within minutes and reducing the time required to assess insurance applications.

> AI Underwriter uses a chatbot to provide preliminary indications based on a customer’s financial, medical, occupational and residential information. 

The system indicates whether an application is likely to be accepted, require exclusions or premium loadings, or need additional information before proceeding.

Prudential said financial consultants receive an earlier view of potential underwriting requirements before submitting an application. Consultants can collect more complete information from customers upfront, reducing subsequent requests for documents or clarification.

Previously, a preliminary assessment could take several days before consultants learned which additional information was required, according to the insurer.
